about.description: The story, goals and contact details of Alper Temiz and Hamza Taşbay, the developers of PDA.
about.lead: Hello! We are Alper Temiz and Hamza Taşbay, fourth-year Software Engineering students at Doğuş University.

journey.title: Our journey
paragraphs: We set out on this road as two friends to close one of the industry's big gaps: a free project management platform. In many tools, important features sit behind paid plans, or you have to depend on paid subscriptions. We wanted to build an alternative that anyone can use without paying.

pda.title: What is PDA?
paragraphs: We develop PDA as open source. Students and small software companies can, if they wish, set up the whole thing on their own computers or servers and run it themselves. Our aim is for you, our dear friends, to achieve great things without facing high fees.

goal.title: Our goal
paragraphs: Our biggest goal is not to become one of those projects that are built and then set aside. With the support of you, our dear users and friends, we want to take PDA to the next level.

Rather than depending on paid subscriptions, we want to lead the industry through open source projects, and instead of an approach where only paid features stand out, we stand for a free one that aims at togetherness across the industry.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Answers about getting started with PDA, accounts, projects, teams, privacy and support.

questions.question: What is PDA and who is it for?
questions.answer: PDA (Project Delivery Assistant) is developed for students and teams that want to manage project delivery in a shared workspace. You can track project information, success criteria, teams, tasks and calendar items.

questions.question: What features does PDA have?
questions.answer: PDA includes project creation, members and project roles, teams, success criteria, tasks (list, board and task pool), sprints, labels, a calendar with reminders, in-app notifications, messaging with project members, and linking a public GitHub repository to browse it. You can group projects under organizations if you like. PDA is under active development, so features may change over time.

questions.question: Do I need to install an application?
questions.answer: PDA is a web application. You can access the hosted service in a current browser. Its responsive interface also adapts to phones and tablets.

questions.question: Is PDA free?
questions.answer: PDA is developed as free, open-source software. Our aim is that core features never sit behind a paid plan. If you run it on your own server, the server and hosting costs are yours.

questions.question: Can I run PDA on my own computer or server?
questions.answer: Yes. PDA is open source and can run on your own infrastructure. The backend and database start with Docker, and the interface runs with Next.js. The steps are in the README file in the GitHub repository. On your own installation, storing and backing up the data is your responsibility.

questions.question: Which license is PDA released under?
questions.answer: Apache License 2.0. It allows you to use, modify and distribute the software, and sets conditions such as keeping the copyright and license notices. You can find a summary and the full text on the License page.

questions.question: How do I create an account?
questions.answer: Open the registration link on the sign-in screen and fill in the e-mail, nickname and password fields. A six-digit verification code is sent to your e-mail address; once you enter it your account is activated and you are signed in. The registration form links to the KVKK Privacy Notice and the Privacy Policy; these are information, and there is no separate consent checkbox.

questions.question: Can I sign in with Google or GitHub?
questions.answer: You can use Google or GitHub when that provider is enabled in the hosted service. An existing account with the same email is not automatically merged; linking may require signing in to your existing account first.

questions.question: How do I create my first project?
questions.answer: After signing in, use the create project action in Projects. Fill in the name, type and required fields; you can also add technology, description and logo details. You become the first project manager of the project you create.

questions.question: What is an organization, and do I have to use one?
questions.answer: An organization is a group that keeps related projects together, for example for a club or a delivery team. It is optional; you can also keep projects independent. Only the owner can edit an organization. An archived organization no longer accepts new projects, and archiving cannot be undone.

questions.question: How do project membership and team membership differ?
questions.answer: Project membership controls access and project roles. Teams organise work within a project. Joining a team does not itself grant manager permissions; actions are checked against project roles.

questions.question: How do I invite my teammates?
questions.answer: Create a team in the project's Teams area and use the add member or invitation action. Project managers can invite a user or an email address. Each invitation belongs to a team and must be accepted by its recipient.

questions.question: Where can I accept or reject invitations?
questions.answer: Registered users can review incoming invitations in Invitations. An external invitation link may lead through registration or sign-in. Respond with the intended account; ask the project manager for a new invitation if yours has expired or been cancelled.

questions.question: Can everyone see my projects?
questions.answer: Creating an account does not grant access to other users' projects. Project data is shown according to active membership and permissions. Some information, such as your email and username, is visible to members you work with; a public GitHub repository may already be publicly accessible on GitHub.

questions.question: Are success criteria the same as tasks?
questions.answer: Success criteria are a checklist of delivery goals. Tasks track work, assignments and statuses. Completing a criterion does not automatically complete tasks; the two areas are separate.

questions.question: What are sprints, the board and the task pool for?
questions.answer: A sprint splits work into time boxes and shows progress on a burndown chart. The board lets you drag tasks between status columns; you can only drop them on allowed transitions. The task pool lists tasks nobody has been assigned yet; a task you take on is assigned to you.

questions.question: Does the GitHub connection change my code?
questions.answer: The current repository connection reads a public GitHub repository and displays recent commits. It does not commit code or open pull requests. Private repositories are outside this connection's scope.

questions.question: I forgot my password. What should I do?
questions.answer: Use the Forgot password link on the sign-in screen. A code is sent to your e-mail address; enter it and choose a new password. E-mail depends on the service's configuration; check your inbox and spam folder. For the password of your Google or GitHub account, use that provider's recovery flow.

questions.question: What does Remember me store?
questions.answer: This option only remembers your email address in this browser. It does not store your password or extend your session. Avoid it on shared devices; turn it off on a subsequent sign-in to clear the remembered email.

questions.question: How do I delete my account or get access to my data?
questions.answer: You can delete your account yourself on the account screen: you confirm with a one-time link sent to your e-mail and your own sign-in credentials, and the account is anonymised at once. If you own a project or an organisation, you must first transfer ownership or delete it. For requests such as access, correction or export of your data, choose the category “KVKK / data request” in the contact form or write to pdassistant.info@gmail.com; we reply within 30 days at the latest. Details are in the KVKK Privacy Notice and the Privacy Policy.

questions.question: Which languages does PDA support?
questions.answer: The interface offers Turkish, English and German. Use the controls at the top to change language and light/dark theme preferences.

questions.question: How can I report a bug or accessibility barrier?
questions.answer: Use the form on the Contact page to send the page address, expected behaviour and reproduction steps. General development suggestions can also be shared in the GitHub repository. Do not post personal data, passwords, verification codes or vulnerability details in public issues.

questions.question: Can I contribute to the project?
questions.answer: Yes, contributions are welcome. You can open an issue, suggest a feature or submit a change in the GitHub repository. If you would like to reach us directly, our contact details are on the About us page.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: Which information PDA uses and why, who can see it, how long it is kept, how to delete your account and the GDPR information for visitors in the EU/EEA.

sections.title: Scope and who is responsible
paragraphs: This policy covers the account, project, team, task, chat, calendar and other features of the PDA web application. When you go to external GitHub or Google pages, the privacy terms of that service apply.
The data controllers are Hamza Taşbay and Alper Temiz, natural persons and maintainers of the open-source PDA project. You can reach us through the contact form or at pdassistant.info@gmail.com.
The detailed information under the Turkish Law No. 6698 (legal bases, transfers, your rights) is in the KVKK Privacy Notice; this policy is a user-oriented summary of the same information.

sections.title: Which information is used?
paragraphs: Depending on the features you use, the following information is kept. Passwords are not stored in plain text; they are protected by a one-way password hash.
items: Account: e-mail, nickname, account status, registration times, the ID of a linked external sign-in provider if any; first and last name (on accounts created through an invitation); optional profile photo.
Two-factor authentication (optional): the authenticator secret is stored encrypted, backup codes as hashes.
Projects and teams: projects, memberships, roles, invitations, accept or decline responses, project logo and banner, organisations and their images.

Work content: tasks, comments, file attachments, time entries, success criteria, calendar entries and reminders, project chat messages (with replies and reactions), in-app notifications and the notification history, only for the features you use.
Session: session times, browser/device information and secure session verification records. The network address is used for request rate limiting.
Support messages: the name, (optional) last name, e-mail address, category and message you write in the contact form.
Visit analytics (only with your consent): an anonymous visitor and session ID, page type, source of the visit, active time, whether certain buttons were clicked and the type of an error.

sections.title: What the information is used for
paragraphs: Account information is used for signing you in and protecting your account; project, team and task data is used to provide your shared workspace. Invitations and notifications are delivered to the person concerned. Controls such as sessions, rate limiting and bot traps aim to reduce unauthorised access and abuse. Support messages are used to answer you.
Visit analytics is used only with your consent, to understand anonymously how the site is used and where errors occur. It is not linked to your account.
Do not add special categories of personal data, passwords or unnecessary information about other people to project descriptions, comments, chat and files.

sections.title: Who can see it?
paragraphs: Workspace content is limited by project membership and role permissions. Authorised project members can see your e-mail and nickname in team lists; the project chat is visible to the project's members. The recipient of an invitation can see the invitation preview shown to them.

Only the PDA administrator can see your support messages. The administrator account can see the account list (e-mail, nickname, status), session records and support requests, and can disable accounts. Administrator actions are written to the administration audit log.

When you choose Google/GitHub sign-in, authentication takes place with that provider; the repository connection reads GitHub's public repository information. Your data is not sold and not shared for advertising.

sections.title: Account deletion and anonymisation
paragraphs: You can delete your account yourself on the account screen. The action is confirmed with a short-lived one-time link sent to your e-mail and your own sign-in credentials.
The moment the account is deleted it is anonymised: the e-mail address, name, nickname and password hash are erased, all sessions are closed and project memberships end. This cannot be undone.

If you own a project or an organisation, you must transfer ownership or delete the project/organisation before deleting your account. The administrator account cannot delete itself. After deletion, the account may still appear with an anonymised identity in other users' project records (for example in task history).
An administrator can disable an account for misuse or security reasons; sessions are then closed and sign-in is blocked, and no data is deleted.

sections.title: Cookies and browser preferences
paragraphs: PDA uses no advertising cookies or third-party tracking tools; fonts are loaded from PDA's own server. Session and security cookies are necessary for the application to work. Visit analytics runs only with your explicit choice and is off by default.
Every cookie and storage entry is listed with its purpose and duration in the Cookie Policy; you can change your choice there or with the “Manage cookie preferences” link at the bottom of the page.

sections.title: Service providers and transfers abroad
paragraphs: E-mails are sent through Gmail SMTP (Google, USA). The optional Google/GitHub sign-in and the GitHub repository features connect to the respective providers (USA). The hosting provider has not been chosen yet; this policy will be updated once it is.

Details of these transfers (recipients, country, which data goes where) and their current status under Article 9 of the Law are in the “Recipients and transfers abroad” section of the KVKK Privacy Notice and in the GDPR sections below; the controllers track compliance of these transfers.

sections.title: Retention periods

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: PDA keeps session tokens in HttpOnly cookies, stores passwords as one-way hashes, encrypts two-factor secrets, checks project permissions on the server and protects administrator access with a separate two-factor sign-in. The contact form uses bot traps that send no data to a third party instead of a CAPTCHA.
These measures are not an absolute security guarantee. On shared devices, sign out when you are done and consider enabling two-factor authentication.

sections.title: Children
paragraphs: PDA is not directed at children. Minors should use PDA with the knowledge of their legal representative.

sections.title: GDPR: controller and contact (Art. 13(1)(a)–(b))
paragraphs: For visitors in the European Union or the European Economic Area, the following information is given under Articles 13 and 14 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). The controllers are Hamza Taşbay and Alper Temiz, natural persons and maintainers of the open-source PDA project, based in Türkiye. Contact: the contact form or pdassistant.info@gmail.com. No data protection officer has been appointed.

sections.title: GDPR: purposes and legal bases (Art. 6)
paragraphs: We process personal data on the following bases.
items: Art. 6(1)(b), contract: creating your account, authenticating you and providing the workspace you ask for under the Terms of Use. Providing the e-mail address, nickname and password is necessary for this; without it no account can be created.

Art. 6(1)(f), legitimate interests: security of accounts and systems, preventing abuse (sessions, rate limiting, bot traps, administration audit log) and answering contact-form messages. Our interest is to run a secure service and to reply to the people who write to us; you can object (see your rights).

Art. 6(1)(a), consent: optional visit analytics, including button-click and error events, and only after you opt in in the cookie layer. You can withdraw consent at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing before withdrawal.
Art. 6(1)(c), legal obligation: answering requests of data subjects and authorities and keeping records where the law requires it.
closing: We do not use automated decision-making or profiling that produces legal or similarly significant effects on you (Art. 22). We do not intentionally process special categories of data (Art. 9).

sections.title: GDPR: recipients and international transfers (Chapter V)
paragraphs: Recipients are the project members you work with, Google (Gmail SMTP for e-mail; optional Google sign-in), GitHub (optional sign-in; repository features) and, once chosen, the hosting provider. The controllers themselves are located in Türkiye, a third country without a European Commission adequacy decision.

Personal data is transferred to the USA, to Google LLC (Gmail SMTP; optional Google sign-in) and GitHub, Inc. (GitHub API; optional GitHub sign-in). Verification and reset codes and notifications about contact-form messages are sent through Gmail; sign-in identifiers go to Google or GitHub only if you choose that sign-in; repository metadata requests go to GitHub when you use the repository feature. The optional sign-ins and the repository feature can be avoided; you can also register with e-mail and password. The controllers track the compliance of these transfers with Chapter V GDPR and Art. 9 KVKK (appropriate safeguards such as standard contractual clauses under Art. 46) and will update this text as such safeguards are put in place. This text does not claim that any specific safeguard or contract is already in place.

sections.title: GDPR: storage period (Art. 13(2)(a))

sections.title: GDPR: your rights and complaints (Art. 15–21, 77)
paragraphs: You have the right of access (Art. 15), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18), data portability (Art. 20) and objection to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21), and the right to withdraw consent at any time (Art. 7(3)). kvkk.title: KVKK Privacy Notice

sections.title: Data controllers and scope
paragraphs: This notice informs you, under Article 10 of the Turkish Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK), about the personal data processed when you use PDA · Project Delivery Assistant (PDA).

The data controllers are Hamza Taşbay and Alper Temiz, the maintainers of the open-source PDA project. Both are natural persons; PDA is not run on behalf of a company or commercial business, so there is no trade name, MERSİS number or registered e-mail (KEP) address.
You can reach the controllers through the contact form on this site or at pdassistant.info@gmail.com. How to submit a personal-data request is described under “How to apply”.

This notice is not a request for consent. The only processing that relies on explicit consent is the optional visit analytics; you decide on it separately and freely in the cookie layer (see the Cookie Policy).

sections.title: Data processed and how it is collected
paragraphs: Data is collected electronically and partly automatically through the registration and sign-in forms, the screens and forms of the application, the contact form, the cookie layer, project members who invite you and, if you choose it, Google or GitHub sign-in.
items: Identity and contact: e-mail address and nickname; first and last name (only on accounts created through a project invitation, entered by the inviting person, and in the contact form if you write it); optional profile photo.

Account security: a one-way hash of your password (the password itself is not stored); hashes of verification and reset codes; if you enable it, two-factor data (the secret is stored encrypted, backup codes as hashes); the ID of a linked Google/GitHub account; session records (session times, browser/device information). For administrator actions an audit log is kept that contains only account IDs, action type, time and outcome.

Workspace content: projects, teams, organisations, tasks, comments, file attachments, project chat messages, in-app notifications, invitations, calendar entries and reminders, only for the features you use.
Support requests: the name, (optional) last name, e-mail address, category and message you write in the contact form.
Operational security: network address information used for request rate limiting and the bot-trap fields of the contact form.

Visit analytics (only with your explicit consent): a randomly generated anonymous visitor and session ID, the type of page visited, the source of the visit, active time, whether certain buttons (register, sign in, contact submission, source-code link) were clicked and the type of an error that occurred in the application. No IP address or browser information is stored for analytics; only the page type is recorded, not the page address.
closing: Do not enter special categories of personal data (health, religion, race, biometric data and the like) into PDA; it is not designed to process them.

closing: Notice and consent are separate: reading this notice or registering does not mean you have given explicit consent to analytics. Declining analytics does not affect your use of PDA.

sections.title: Recipients and transfers abroad
paragraphs: Your personal data is not sold and not shared for advertising. It is passed on to the following recipients, for the stated purpose and to the extent necessary.
items: Project members: workspace content and membership information (e-mail, nickname, profile photo) are shown to the authorised members of the project for working together; an invitation preview is shown to the recipient of the invitation.

E-mail service (Google, USA): verification codes, password reset, invitation and notification e-mails and contact-form messages are sent through Gmail SMTP. Contact-form messages are also delivered to the PDA inbox (pdassistant.info@gmail.com, Gmail).

Sign-in with Google and GitHub (optional): if you choose it, authentication takes place at the provider (USA); PDA receives the basic account information needed for sign-in (account ID, e-mail address, name).
GitHub API (repository features): when you connect a public repository to a project, repository information and recent commits are read from the GitHub API (USA).

Hosting provider: the hosting provider for PDA's production environment has not been chosen yet. Once it is chosen, this notice will be updated with its name, the data location and any transfer abroad.
Authorities: public bodies and authorities, where a legal obligation arises.
closing: Transfers abroad (Art. 9): personal data is transferred to the following recipients in the USA: Google LLC (Gmail SMTP and optional Google sign-in) and GitHub, Inc. (GitHub API and optional GitHub sign-in). Verification and reset codes and notifications about contact-form messages are sent through Gmail; your sign-in identifiers go to Google or GitHub only if you choose that sign-in; repository metadata requests go to GitHub when you use the repository feature.

The optional Google/GitHub sign-in and the repository features can be avoided; you can also register with e-mail and password. Sending e-mail, however, is necessary for the service to work. The controllers track compliance of these transfers with Article 9 of the Law (appropriate safeguards such as standard contracts and the notification to the Board) and will update this text as these safeguards are put in place. This text does not state that any specific safeguard or contract is already in place.

sections.title: Retention periods
paragraphs: Data is kept for as long as the purpose requires and is then deleted or anonymised. Deletions run automatically.

table.caption: Retention periods
rows: The account is anonymised the moment it is deleted: e-mail address, name, nickname and password hash are erased, sessions are closed, project and organisation memberships end. An owner of a project or organisation must transfer ownership or delete it before deleting their account.
Contact-form status records and stored support messages (name, e-mail, category, message)

Deleted automatically. The e-mail copies delivered to the PDA inbox (Gmail) are cleaned up manually by the controllers at least once a year: messages older than 12 months are deleted at the latest in the yearly cleanup, and immediately on request (data request via the contact-form category “KVKK / data request” or by e-mail).
Visit analytics (sessions, page views, button clicks and error events)
Deleted automatically. The anonymous visitor ID is renewed in your browser every 12 months and removed at once when you withdraw your analytics consent.
Administration audit log (account IDs, action type, time and outcome only)

closing: Deleting your account does not by itself remove other users' project records (for example task history); these records may remain with an anonymised account ID. If a legal retention duty arises, the relevant information is kept for that period. The backup and hosting arrangements will be added to this notice once the hosting provider is chosen.

sections.title: Your rights under the Law
paragraphs: Under Article 11 of the Law you can apply to the controller to exercise the following rights.
items: To learn whether your personal data is processed and, if so, to request information.
To learn the purpose of processing and whether the data is used in line with that purpose.
To know the third parties in Türkiye or abroad to whom the data is transferred.
To request correction of incomplete or inaccurate data.
To request deletion or destruction of the data under the conditions of the Law, and to request that corrections and deletions be notified to recipients.
To object to a result against you that arises solely from analysis by automated systems.
To claim compensation for damage caused by unlawful processing.
closing: You can update your profile yourself on the account screen and delete your account there. Exporting your data is not yet a feature inside the application; it is provided on request.

sections.title: How to apply
paragraphs: To exercise your rights, choose one of two ways: select the category “KVKK / data request” in the contact form, or send an e-mail to pdassistant.info@gmail.com.

State your name, the e-mail address linked to your account and your request clearly. Sending from the e-mail address linked to your account is usually enough to confirm the application is yours; if necessary we may ask for proportionate additional verification. Do not send passwords, verification codes or invitation links.

We conclude your application, depending on its nature, as soon as possible and at the latest within 30 days, free of charge. If the process requires a separate cost, the fee in the tariff set by the Board may be charged.
If you find the answer insufficient, you can complain to the Personal Data Protection Board within 30 days of learning the answer and in any case within 60 days of the application date.

sections.title: Data security and breach notification
paragraphs: Passwords are stored as one-way hashes, session tokens are kept in HttpOnly cookies, two-factor secrets are encrypted, project permissions are checked on the server and administrator access is protected by a separate two-factor sign-in. These measures are not an absolute security guarantee.

If personal data is obtained unlawfully by others, we notify the Board and the data subjects affected as soon as possible under Article 12 of the Law (within 72 hours, as required by a Board decision).

sections.title: VERBİS registration
paragraphs: The data controllers are natural persons and run PDA as a non-commercial open-source project. The controllers (Hamza Taşbay and Alper Temiz) have no employees and no company or commercial revenue, so they are below the thresholds set by the Personal Data Protection Board for registration (fewer than 50 employees per year and an annual financial balance-sheet total below the amount set by the Board).

Accordingly, there is currently no obligation to register in the Data Controllers' Registry (VERBİS), and there is no VERBİS registration number. If the obligation arises, it will be fulfilled within the legal period and this notice will be updated.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.description: PDA's accessibility goal, its current status, known limitations, how it is evaluated and how to report a barrier.

sections.title: Our goal
paragraphs: We aim for PDA to be accessible on different screen sizes and for different needs. Our target standard is WCAG 2.2 level AA. Accessibility is continuing work that must be checked again as the product develops.

sections.title: Current status and evaluation
paragraphs: This statement is based on an evaluation dated 10 October 2026. There is no formal WCAG audit of PDA by an independent body; we therefore do not declare full conformance, and this page is not a certificate.

Our own methods: the public pages (landing, sign-in, registration, password reset, about, FAQ, the legal information pages, accessibility and licence) are scanned automatically with axe against the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A/AA rules in three languages, in light and dark themes, at phone and desktop widths (the a11y-public test in the end-to-end suite). Forms, menus, the contact and information pages are also checked with automated tests for keyboard use, focus ring and screen width.
Automated tools catch only part of the problems; manual verification with real screen readers and different browser combinations is an ongoing need.

sections.title: Keyboard use
paragraphs: You can move between links and controls with Tab and Shift+Tab and activate the focused link or button with Enter. The Skip to content link at the start of the page helps you reach the main content.
You can open and close FAQ questions with Enter or Space. In menus and dialogs you can use the application's existing keyboard controls and close supported windows with Escape.

sections.title: Appearance and reading preferences
paragraphs: The top of the page has language and theme controls. You can choose a light, dark or system theme and use Turkish, English or German interface text.
You can use your browser's zoom. When the reduced-motion preference on your device is on, application animations are reduced. On narrow screens, content and footer links stack.

sections.title: Meaningful content and assistive technology
paragraphs: On information pages, headings, main content, tables and navigation areas are structured with meaningful HTML elements. The GitHub links in the footer have an accessible name that includes the person's name; decorative icons are hidden from screen readers. Form errors are associated with their field.

sections.title: Known limitations
paragraphs: The following areas are not yet fully accessible or have not been verified.
items: The analytics charts and visual summaries in the administration panel have not been verified with a screen reader; this area is open to the administrator only.
The Google and GitHub sign-in pages belong to those providers; their accessibility is not under PDA's control.
The accessibility tags of the CV PDF files that can be downloaded from the About page have not been verified.
The signed-in screens of the application (project boards, drag and drop, the calendar) have not been comprehensively verified with screen readers and different browser combinations.

sections.title: Report a barrier
paragraphs: If you cannot use a page or a process, tell us through the contact form with the category “Accessibility” or by writing to pdassistant.info@gmail.com. Give the page address, what you wanted to do, your browser/device and, if any, the assistive technology you use.

We reply to reports within 30 days at the latest and, where possible, provide the content in an alternative format. If you share screenshots, cover personal data and secrets. You do not need to explain a medical condition to make a report.

cookies.manageText: You can turn analytics on or off at any time. When you turn it off, no new measurements are sent and the analytics identifiers in this browser are deleted.

sections.title: What are cookies?
paragraphs: Cookies are small records that a website stores in your browser. On this page, “cookie” also covers browser local storage (localStorage) and session storage (sessionStorage) used for the same purpose.
PDA uses no advertising cookies, no profiling, no third-party tracking tools and no browser fingerprinting. Fonts are loaded from PDA's own server.

sections.title: Categories
paragraphs: PDA uses two consent categories. The necessary category is always on and cannot be switched off; appearance and usage preferences are treated as the functional part of this category (see the reasoning below). The analytics category runs only with your explicit choice and is off by default.
items: Necessary: sign-in, session security, protection against forged requests, language choice, temporary verification steps and the record of this choice.
Functional preferences: remember a setting you made yourself (theme, layout, remembered e-mail) in this browser.
Analytics: anonymous measurement of page type, source of the visit, active time, clicks on certain buttons and the type of errors.

sections.title: Necessary cookies and storage
paragraphs: The following records are required for the service to work and are used regardless of your analytics choice. All are managed by PDA (first party). Durations depend on the service configuration; the values given are the defaults. If you block them in your browser settings, sign-in and session features will not work.

sections.title: Appearance and usage preferences
paragraphs: The following records only remember settings you made yourself in this browser. They do not measure your visit, are not sent to the server and have no tracking purpose. Without them we could not provide the appearance and settings you chose on your next visit; we therefore treat them as functional records necessary to provide the service you asked for and do not ask for separate consent. closing: <user ID> is the random internal ID of your account; it is not your e-mail address or name.

sections.title: Analytics (off by default)
paragraphs: Analytics collects no data and creates no identifier until you say “Accept all” or switch Analytics on in the preferences window. It also stays off as long as you have not decided. When on, the measurement is kept on PDA's own server; there is no third-party analytics tool.

No name, e-mail, message content, token, password, account ID, IP address, browser information or browser fingerprint is collected. Even if you are signed in, the measurement is not linked to your account.
Collected analytics records are deleted automatically after 12 months. The anonymous visitor ID is renewed in your browser every 12 months; a new record is not linked to the old ID.
Operating figures such as the number of accounts, active and ended accounts and submitted contact forms do not depend on your analytics consent; they are calculated from the service's own records.
items: The type of page visited (for example “project page”); project names, user IDs or address queries are not recorded.
The source of the visit: direct, search engine, another site (domain only) or a campaign link (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign).
Active time on the site; time while the tab is in the background or the window is out of focus is not counted.

Button clicks: only whether buttons from a fixed list were clicked (the register and sign-in buttons on the landing page and in the header, submission of the registration and contact forms, the source-code link); nothing about who clicked or what you typed is recorded.

Error events: when an error occurs in the application, only the error type (rendering, file loading, unhandled promise rejection or network) and the page type are recorded. No error message, detail, address or identifier is recorded. The same error is reported once per session.

Randomly generated anonymous visitor and session IDs: pda:analytics-visitor and pda:analytics-session (localStorage). The session ID is renewed after 30 minutes of inactivity. Both are deleted when you withdraw consent.

sections.title: Changing and withdrawing your choice
paragraphs: You can open the preferences window at any time with the “Manage cookie preferences” link at the bottom of the page or the button on this page. When you turn analytics off, new measurements stop at once, button-click and error events are no longer sent, and the analytics identifiers in this browser are deleted. Because the identifier is deleted, records collected earlier can no longer be linked to you; they are deleted automatically after 12 months.
Effect of withdrawal: necessary cookies keep working; no feature other than analytics is restricted. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.

The choice belongs to this browser and is not tied to your account: you need to choose separately in another browser or device. When the cookie practice changes in a meaningful way, the consent version is raised and your choice is asked again.

sections.title: Third parties
paragraphs: PDA has no advertising or third-party analytics cookies. When you sign in with Google or GitHub, your browser is redirected to that provider's page and the provider's own cookie and privacy terms apply. Verification, invitation and contact e-mails are sent from the server and leave no cookie in your browser.

sections.title: Legal basis and contact
paragraphs: Storing or reading information on your device is subject to your consent unless it is strictly necessary to provide a service you expressly requested. Necessary and functional records fall under that exception: under Turkish law they rest on Article 5/2(c) and (f) of the KVKK; in the EU, Article 5(3) of the ePrivacy Directive and its national implementations apply, for visitors in Germany § 25(2) No. 2 TDDDG (formerly TTDSG). Analytics rests only on your explicit consent (Art. 5/1 KVKK; Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR; § 25(1) TDDDG). The regulator's cookie guide is linked in the official references below.

Send questions about cookies through the contact form or to pdassistant.info@gmail.com. The data controllers are Hamza Taşbay and Alper Temiz (details in the KVKK Privacy Notice and the Privacy Policy).

users.title: Users
users.description: View the accounts on the platform; end a membership or re-activate it. Accounts are never deleted.

empty.title: No users found
empty.description: Change your search or the status filter.

terminate.title: End the membership of {name}
terminate.description: This account is disabled immediately: all open sessions end, it cannot sign in and its chat connections are closed. The account and its projects, tasks and history are not deleted. This is reversible: an administrator can open the account again with "Re-activate".
terminate.confirmLabel: To confirm, type the username exactly: {name}

reactivate.title: Re-activate the account of {name}
reactivate.description: The account can sign in again. Earlier sessions do not come back; the user has to sign in again.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: An overview of visits, registrations, accounts and contact requests. Traffic comes only from the anonymous data of visitors who allowed cookies; registrations, accounts and contact requests come from the service's own records.

range.label: Date range
range.invalid: The start date cannot be after the end date and the range can be at most 366 days.

traffic.sourceNote: Direct: entries with no referring site and no campaign parameter. A shared link is only told apart when a reliable campaign (UTM) parameter is present.
traffic.noReferrers: No referring sites in this range.
traffic.noCampaigns: No visits through campaign links in this range.
traffic.empty: No data from visitors who allowed cookies in this range.

users.note: An active account does not mean an online user; it is the number of accounts whose status is active.

contact.label: Requests
contact.note: Only successfully delivered messages are counted; message content is not shown here.

pages.note: Pages appear as route templates (for example /projects/[slug]); no ids or query text are stored. Only from visitors who allowed cookies.

flows.note: The first page of a session and the second page it opened next.
flows.title: Page flows

notFound.note: Visits to an address that does not exist.

ctas.note: Clicks on call-to-action buttons and links; each click carries only a fixed button id.
ctas.title: CTA clicks

conversion.note: A conversion is a session that submitted the registration form. The rate is the share among sessions that started in the range.

errors.note: Only from the browsers of visitors who allowed cookies. No error text, user or address detail is collected; only the kind of error and the page template.

userDetail.title: User details

banner.label: Cookie preferences
banner.title: Your cookie choices
banner.description: PDA uses necessary cookies and browser storage to keep you signed in. You can also allow analytics, which measures how the site is used without identifying you. Analytics is off by default and you can change your choice at any time.

dialog.title: Cookie preferences
dialog.description: Choose which categories to allow. Your choice is stored only in this browser and does not depend on your account.

necessary.title: Necessary
necessary.description: Required for sign-in, session security, protection against forged requests, your language and the record of this choice. PDA does not work without them, so they cannot be switched off.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: Measures, anonymously, the type of page visited, where the visit came from, the time actively spent on the site, whether certain buttons were clicked and the type of any error. It is not linked to your account and collects no name, email or content. Off by default.

notice.title: Before you send
notice.text: The data controllers are Hamza Taşbay and Alper Temiz. Your message is processed to reply to you; it is kept for 12 months and delivered by email to the PDA inbox (Gmail); the copies in the inbox are cleaned up manually at least once a year (messages older than 12 months are deleted at the latest in the yearly cleanup, and immediately on request). Do not write your password, verification code or the secret parts of an invitation link.
